intro.text: Gach Alley is only about 128 metres long, lined with small cafes and guesthouses, and midway along it stands a communal house with a stele dated 1430.

nodes.name: Cafe No.1
nodes.summary: A cafe at number 1, right at the eastern entrance. This is where the walk starts.
nodes.story: The walk starts at the coffee shop marked at number one, by the eastern end of Gạch Alley. The available route data gives its location only, so I will not add a story about the shop. Continue along the alley to the marker at number four A.
nodes.caption: A cafe at number 1, right at the eastern entrance. This is where the walk starts.

nodes.name: Ta Coffee 4
nodes.summary: A small coffee shop at 4A, about thirty steps from the entrance.
nodes.story: Next is Ta Cà Phê at number four A, listed in the route data about thirty steps from the alley entrance. I use that only as an orientation cue; I found no independent source for a longer account of the shop. Farther along, the route reaches Thanh Hà Communal House at number ten Gạch Alley.
nodes.caption: A small coffee shop at 4A, about thirty steps from the entrance.

nodes.name: Thanh Ha Communal House
nodes.summary: A communal house for Tran Luu, holding a stele dated 1430 that the press calls the oldest surviving in Hanoi.
nodes.story: Thanh Hà Communal House at number ten Gạch Alley is dedicated to Trần Lựu. Accounts tell a legend of his service at Vũ Ninh, but it remains a story passed down rather than an event I can verify. The house holds the Thanh Hà Ngọc Phả Bi Ký stele, erected in the year fourteen thirty; press reports call it Hanoi's oldest surviving stele. Sources list its festivals on the fourth day of the fourth lunar month and the fifteenth day of the ninth lunar month.
nodes.caption: Thanh Ha communal house for Tran Luu, holding a stele dated 1430 at 10 Gach Alley.

nodes.name: Cafe 20
nodes.summary: A coffee shop at number 20, near the western end.
nodes.story: Near the western end of Gạch Alley, the route data marks a coffee shop at number twenty. I found no source specific to the shop, so I keep this as an orientation point only. The available information does not confirm its history, menu, or opening hours.
nodes.caption: A coffee shop at number 20, near the western end.

nodes.name: Cau Dong Pagoda
nodes.summary: Cầu Đông Pagoda on Hàng Đường Street, with wooden statues identified as Trần Thủ Độ and Trần Thị Dung.
nodes.story: A newspaper places Cầu Đông Pagoda at number thirty-eight B Hàng Đường Street. It reports that the pagoda has two wooden seated statues identified as Grand Chancellor Trần Thủ Độ and Trần Thị Dung; their origins and meaning remain unknown. Researchers quoted in the article date the statues to the first half of the eighteenth century. The report confirms the street address, but does not establish how close the pagoda is to Gạch Alley's western entrance.
nodes.caption: Cầu Đông Pagoda is at 38B Hàng Đường Street; its position relative to Gạch Alley's western end is unverified.
